subject: Microbiology
subtopic: Q fever: zoonotic exposure, intracellular organism, acute/chronic disease, diagnosis, treatment and prevention
concept: Q fever is a zoonotic infection caused by Coxiella burnetii, commonly acquired by inhaling contaminated aerosols from infected livestock and their birth products.

content.definition: Q fever is a zoonotic infection caused by Coxiella burnetii, commonly acquired by inhaling contaminated aerosols from infected livestock and their birth products.
content.explanation: C. burnetii is an obligate intracellular bacterium adapted to survive in acidic intracellular compartments. Acute infection may produce a febrile systemic illness; a minority develop chronic infection, classically involving endocarditis in people with risk factors.
content.mechanism: C. burnetii is an obligate intracellular bacterium adapted to survive in acidic intracellular compartments. Acute infection may produce a febrile systemic illness; a minority develop chronic infection, classically involving endocarditis in people with risk factors.
content.structure: Clinically important organism-specific structural and biologic features are summarized in the explanation and terminology fields.
content.function: The pathogen's biologic properties determine transmission, tissue tropism, clinical manifestations and diagnostic strategy.
causes: Inhalation of contaminated dust or aerosols
Exposure to infected goats, sheep or cattle and birth products
Contaminated environments; direct animal contact is an important risk
effects: Acute Q fever: fever, headache, myalgia, fatigue; pneumonia or hepatitis can occur
Chronic Q fever: persistent infection, especially endocarditis or vascular infection in high-risk patients
content.clinical_relevance: This is an official Hematology microbiology syllabus organism/disease. Coxiella burnetii and Q Fever should be interpreted using current diagnostic and treatment guidance.
content.diagnosis: Diagnosis relies on clinical and exposure context plus serology/PCR according to disease stage; paired serology and phase-specific antibodies are important in interpretation.
content.treatment: Doxycycline is recommended for symptomatic acute Q fever in appropriate patients. Chronic Q fever requires prolonged specialist-guided combination therapy and monitoring.
